profile.name: Naqib Sad Pathan
profile.title: PhD Candidate · Optimal Transport, Computational Biology, Single Cell Data Analysis
profile.about: Doctoral researcher in Electrical Engineering at the University of Virginia advised by Prof. Gustavo K. Rohde in the Imaging and Data Science Laboratory. Research at the intersection of optimal transport, machine learning, mathematical modeling, and computational biology, developing generalizable methods for high-dimensional cellular measurements with applications to flow cytometry, multiplex imaging (4i/cIF), digital pathology, and biomedical discovery.

experience.company: Imaging and Data Science Laboratory (Rohde Lab), University of Virginia
bullets: Conduct research on optimal transport theory, transport-based morphometry (TBM), and mathematical machine learning frameworks for multiplex imaging and high-dimensional single-cell measurements.
Formulate FlowLOT for flow cytometry data, achieving state-of-the-art continuous quantitative prediction of measurable residual disease (MRD) in acute myeloid leukemia (AML).

Lead computational analysis for high-plex iterative indirect immunofluorescence imaging (4i) to map metaphase chromosome spatial architecture and chromosome passenger complex (CPC) dynamics during mitosis.

experience.role: Research Intern — Spatial Proteomics / Computational Biology
bullets: Developed computational autofluorescence correction methods for cyclic immunofluorescence imaging (4i/cIF technique) on Lunaphore COMET to enhance signal fidelity and multiplex biomarker quantification.
Implemented image restoration and quantitative single-cell feature extraction pipelines across complex tissue microenvironments.

experience.company: Chittagong University of Engineering and Technology (CUET)
bullets: Taught undergraduate courses in Digital Signal Processing, Signals and Systems, VLSI Technology, and Microprocessors & Interfacing.
Mentored student research projects and directed laboratory sessions in biomedical signal processing, embedded systems, and computer vision (on study leave for doctoral studies since August 2022).

projects.title: FlowLOT: Optimal Transport for Single-Cell Measurements & AML MRD Prediction
projects.description: FlowLOT is an optimal transport-based framework that represents patient-derived single-cell measurements as empirical cellular distributions and maps them into fixed-length feature embeddings. Unifies high-dimensional classification, interpretable visualization, and continuous quantitative prediction, including measurable residual disease (MRD) estimation in acute myeloid leukemia (AML), within a transparent and mathematically interpretable architecture.

projects.title: Metaphase Chromosome Analysis with Iterative Indirect Immunofluorescence Imaging (4i)
projects.description: Investigates how chromosome passenger complex (CPC) signaling and chromosome condensation are coordinated during mitosis using high-dimensional multiplex imaging. Develops optimal transport-based methods to quantify, visualize, and compare chromosome-scale variation across cell lines, studying how chromosome geometry influences protein localization and chromosomal organization.

projects.title: Quantifying Nuclear Structures in Digital Pathology Using Transport-Based Morphometry (TBM)
projects.description: Develops transport-based morphometry (TBM) methods grounded in optimal transport theory to quantify nuclear chromatin organization directly from microscopy images. By representing nuclei relative to a common template, these methods provide interpretable and robust morphological descriptors that reveal cancer-associated structural variation across tissue types and imaging protocols.

projects.title: Computational Autofluorescence Correction for Cyclic Immunofluorescence (cIF)
projects.description: High-plex cyclic immunofluorescence (cIF) experiments are often affected by tissue autofluorescence and imaging artifacts that distort downstream biological measurements. Developed computational and machine-learning approaches for autofluorescence correction, image restoration, and quantitative analysis of spatial proteomics data on Lunaphore COMET.

projects.title: Biomedical Signal Processing and Clinical Image Analysis
projects.description: Investigations in biomedical signal processing and medical image analysis, including motion-corrupted photoplethysmography (PPG) heart-rate estimation during intense exercise, EEG sleep and motor imagery classification, retinal blood vessel segmentation using modified U-Net architectures, and brain MRI analysis.
